entries.title: W65C02 Hello World computer
entries.description: A W65C02 with an AT28C256 EEPROM, a W65C22 VIA and a 16×2 LCD. Its program is already in the ROM: run it and it types Hello World.

entries.title: Z80A Hello World computer
entries.description: A Z80A with an AT28C256 EEPROM, a W65C22 VIA and a 16×2 LCD. Its program is already in the ROM: run it and it types Hello World.

entries.title: 555 astable oscillator
entries.description: A 555 wired to run on its own: two resistors and a capacitor set how fast the LED flashes.

entries.title: 555 one-shot
entries.description: A 555 wired as a monostable: one press starts a pulse whose length the resistor and capacitor decide.

entries.title: 555 latch
entries.description: A 555 used as a bistable: one button sets it, the other resets it.

entries.title: Speaker tone
entries.description: A 555 oscillator driving a speaker. Run it under Spice Lite to hear the tone.

entries.title: Speaker on a key
entries.description: A tone that sounds only while its key is held.

entries.title: Two-tone siren
entries.description: Two 555s: a slow one switching a fast one between two pitches.

entries.title: LED fade
entries.description: Electrolytic capacitors charging and discharging through the LEDs, so they fade rather than snap on and off.

entries.title: RC timer
entries.description: A capacitor charging through a resistor, read by a CD40106B Schmitt trigger: its output changes a set time after the switch is flipped.

entries.title: LC ringing
entries.description: An inductor and a capacitor ringing each time a CD4040B counter's output kicks them. Watch the ring decay on the analyzer.

entries.title: Diode clipping
entries.description: An AC adapter's wave clipped by a Zener diode and squared by a 74LS14, then divided by a 74LS90 and a 74LS92 to blink the LEDs.

entries.title: Zero-crossing detector
entries.description: An LM358 marks each time the AC wave crosses zero, and a 74LS90 counts the crossings.

entries.title: Schmitt trigger
entries.description: An LM358 with positive feedback turns the AC wave into a clean square, which a 74LS90 counts.

entries.title: Step-down transformer
entries.description: Mains through a step-down transformer: compare the two windings on the analyzer.

entries.title: Op-amp comparator
entries.description: An LM358 comparing a potentiometer against a reference and lighting an LED.

entries.title: Op-amp amplifier
entries.description: An LM358 wired as an amplifier, its gain set by two resistors.

entries.title: Window comparator
entries.description: Two comparators that light the LED only while the input sits between two thresholds.

entries.title: Comparator oscillator
entries.description: An LM339 comparator made to oscillate with an RC network.

entries.title: 5 V regulator under load
entries.description: An LM7805 holding 5 V while an electronic load draws current from it.

entries.title: Adjustable regulator at 3.3 V
entries.description: An LM317 set to 3.3 V by its two resistors.

entries.title: Relay with a transistor driver
entries.description: A transistor switching a relay coil, with a flyback diode across it.

entries.title: Relay without a flyback diode
entries.description: The same relay driver with no diode across the coil: see what the coil does when the transistor turns off.

entries.title: Darlington relay driver
entries.description: A ULN2003A Darlington array driving a relay and LEDs from two switches.

entries.title: Optocoupler isolated switch
entries.description: A 4N35 optocoupler passing a switch's state between two separate supplies.
